name: notes
description: Write up finished work: root-cause analyses, reusable-pattern learnings, release notes, daily task logs, debugging blog posts.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the notes skills.

The authoritative mapping is owned by the sibling repo dEitY719/harness-skills at `references/kimi-tools.md` (dotfiles #1410 F-5). Read it there when a skill names a tool you do not recognise; this repo deliberately keeps no copy. Summary:

- "Ask the user" -> `AskUserQuestion`. `notes:insight` (candidate pick, memory pointer) and `notes:blog-dev-learnings` (title pick) both wait on a real answer.
- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or "explore" (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`.
- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Search contents with `Grep`; match paths with `Glob`.
- Every skill here mines the current conversation for its source material. Kimi Code has no transcript-reading tool: use what is in the live context window, and when that is empty, ask the user for the incident instead of inventing one.
- `notes:rca` and `notes:task-history` may commit (`--commit`, auto-commit). They never push unless the documented env var says so; do not add a push.
- Paths are absolute and outside the current repo for `notes:rca`, `notes:task-history`, and `notes:blog-dev-learnings` ($RCA_REPO_PATH, $TASK_HISTORY_DIR, ~/para/archive/). `notes:insight` and `notes:release-note` write inside the current repo.

interface.shortDescription: Write up what you just built or just fixed
interface.longDescription: Notes bundles the five skills that turn a finished session into a readable document: rca, insight, release-note, task-history, and blog-dev-learnings.
